study.title: Prolonged Repeated Acupuncture Stimulation Induces Habituation Effects in Pain-Related Brain Areas: An fMRI Study
study.study_design: within-subject repeated measures fMRI experiment with prolonged repeated acupuncture stimulation
study.inclusion_criteria: healthy volunteers, right-handed college students, age 21 to 32 years old, 20 males and 20 females; no history of mental, psychiatric or neurological disorders, drug abuse, or abnormality in brain
study.exclusion_criteria: any volunteer who had acupuncture experience in the past three months was excluded; data with head movement greater than 1 mm or 1 degree were excluded (resulting in exclusion of six cases)

arms.dropouts: six cases excluded due to head movement greater than 1 mm or 1 degree

interventions.needle_type_exact: sterile and disposable acupuncture needles (Suzhou Medical Appliance Factory, China)
interventions.manipulation_exact: handles of the needles were connected to an electro-acupuncture machine at frequency of 2 Hz and intensity of 2 mA; once the De-Qi sensation was elicited
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; De-Qi sensation was elicited before connecting to electro-acupuncture machine
interventions.needle_retention_exact: from the time of needle-in to the time of needle-out, lasting more than 40 minutes
interventions.session_duration_exact: more than 40 minutes from the time of needle-in to the time of needle-out
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: one session with three runs (six blocks) of acupuncture fMRI
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: a professional acupuncturist performed all operations of acupuncture
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: subjects were asked not to fall into sleep; asked to relax; ears plugged with cotton balls to reduce audio stimulations; asked to close their eyes and avoid any psychological activities during scanning
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: to investigate cumulative effects of typical clinical application of acupuncture; prolonged acupuncture stimulation suggested to investigate cumulative effects

extraction_notes.note: Figure S1 (activation and deactivation in first, second, third run and total) and Figure S2 (activation and deactivation in each of six blocks) are described but not included in the main PDF text with quantitative data. Coordinate tables for these supplementary figures are not available in the extracted text.

Figure 2 (De-Qi sensation composition) presents data as bar charts by case counts for each sensation grade (None, Mild, Moderate, Severe) for both sides. Exact numeric values cannot be reliably extracted from figure description alone; only the axes labels and general structure are described in text.

Figure 4 (ROI analysis results for four overlapped areas) presents bar graphs of brain response across six blocks for MCC, PCL, SII, and Right Thalamus. Only the Pearson R values are explicitly stated in the text (R=0.94, 0.87, 0.63, 0.84). Exact values per block are from figures, not text tables.

Talairach coordinate sign convention: the paper reports peak coordinates including negative x-values (e.g., -55.5, -61.5) which in Talairach convention typically indicate right hemisphere. However, the paper labels some regions 'R' (right) with negative x coordinates. This is internally consistent with Talairach convention where negative x = right hemisphere. Coordinates have been extracted as reported.

The paper states 'FOV 192 mm×192 mm, matrix 64×64' for fMRI and 'slice thickness/interval 3.0 mm/0.75 mm' from 2D anatomical parameters. Explicit voxel size for fMRI is not separately stated but can be inferred (3×3×3 mm). Not computed; left as reported.
No preprocessing or analysis software package names are reported (e.g., SPM, FSL, AFNI). The paper describes GLM and ANCOVA analyses without naming the software used.
No smoothing kernel size is reported in the methods section.
No normalization template is explicitly named. The coordinate space is stated as Talairach (as labeled in tables and figure captions).
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding assessments were not conducted. No sham acupuncture arm was included. The paper explicitly states the reason for not using sham acupuncture.
Adverse events were not systematically reported in the paper.
No trial registration number is provided.
The depth range reported is '15-20 mm' for needle insertion. A single numeric value cannot be assigned without inferring; therefore depth_mm_numeric is set to null.
Table 1 lists Inferior Parietal Lobule as 'L' (left) hemisphere but the x coordinate is +43.5 which in Talairach convention is left hemisphere. This is internally consistent.

Table 1 lists Middle Temporal Gyrus (37) with coordinates +52.5, +55.5, -6.5 labeled 'L' and another Middle Temporal Gyrus (37) with coordinates +46.5, +64.5, +8.5 also labeled 'L'. Both positive x values indicate left hemisphere in Talairach space. Extracted as reported.

The paper reports the Inferior Parietal Lobule (BA40) in Table 1 as 'L' hemisphere at +43.5 x-coordinate, and SII (BA40) as 'R' at -61.5 x-coordinate. Both are consistent with Talairach convention (positive x = left, negative x = right). Extracted as reported without conversion.

The 'R' hemisphere labels in Table 1 for regions with negative x-coordinates and 'L' hemisphere labels for regions with positive x-coordinates are consistent with Talairach coordinate convention. No conversion was applied.

The paper references Figures S1 and S2 as supplementary information (TIF files) which are not included in the extracted PDF. Complete block-by-block and run-by-run coordinate tables from these figures are unavailable.

The ANCOVA Table 2 coordinates for SII (R) show y=25.5 whereas Table 1 for the same region shows y=+28.5. These are slightly different y-coordinates for the same labeled region, suggesting the ANCOVA peak is at a slightly different location. Both extracted as reported.

The ANCOVA Table 2 Thalamus (R) shows y=16.5, z=11.5 whereas Table 1 Thalamus (R) shows y=+13.5, z=+14.5. These differ slightly between the activation and habituation peak coordinates, consistent with the regions overlapping but not being identical peaks.
